memory_update.text: MP is the reference leader for U.S.-listed rare-earth mine-to-magnet exposure, but high attention means it should be used mainly as a benchmark for qualifying smaller discovery candidates.

USAR is a direct underfollowed candidate for the magnet-capacity layer; survival in later layers depends on proof of commercial output, feedstock provenance, customer qualification, and technology/IP risk resolution.
Energy Fuels is a second-order but strategically relevant underfollowed candidate at the rare-earth oxide and qualified feedstock layer, especially if heavy rare-earth oxides become the chokepoint.

The key research gap is not whether companies announce rare-earth capacity, but whether their oxides, metals, alloys, or magnets are qualified under non-Chinese provenance rules for defense/aerospace customers.

node: Compliant rare-earth magnets and qualified non-Chinese feedstock
summary: Layer 1B expanded the direct public-company universe for the rare-earth magnet compliance node. The strongest direct exposure is not broad mining alone, but companies attempting to control qualified non-Chinese feedstock, oxide separation, metal/alloy conversion, and NdFeB magnet output. MP Materials is the obvious reference leader; USA Rare Earth and Energy Fuels are the more relevant underfollowed public discovery candidates because they sit closer to the magnet/feedstock qualification bottleneck than generic critical-minerals names. NioCorp is included only as a speculative shadow because its rare-earth relevance is plausible but project-stage and needs stronger qualification/offtake evidence.
